sections.title: What's changing on January 11, 2027
text: Amazon has announced an update to its **Product bundling policy** that takes effect on **January 11, 2027**. Under the update, most product bundles listed as a single ASIN must be packaged by the original manufacturer or brand.

Amazon lists exceptions, including bundles covered by a letter of authorization from the brands or manufacturers of all the products in the bundle, bundles in gifting browse nodes and camera product types, and bundles created with Amazon's Virtual Bundles tool (which Amazon says may not yet be available for every store, brand or fulfillment channel). Amazon is also removing some earlier bundle restrictions.
Amazon says bundles that are still noncompliant after January 11 will be deactivated and become listing violations on the seller's Account Health dashboard, and that it will notify sellers by email.
sections.note: Sources: Amazon's announcement [New requirements for product bundles starting January 11](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/seller-forums/discussions/t/da850a57-839d-4e38-a96f-298dbc450b69) on the Amazon Seller Forums (September 2026) and Amazon's [Product bundling policy](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/help/hub/reference/external/G200442350) page. Last checked October 21, 2026. Amazon can change its policies at any time, so always confirm in your own Seller Central account.

sections.title: What we check
items: Whether a bundle looks like it was put together by the seller rather than packaged by the original manufacturer or brand

Whether one of Amazon's listed exceptions may apply: a letter of authorization from the brands or manufacturers of all the products in the bundle, a gifting browse node, a camera product type, or a virtual bundle made with Amazon's Virtual Bundles tool

Amazon's bundle listing basics: the word "Bundle" in the title; a description that says it's a bundle and names every item; a first bullet point that says it's a bundle of a stated number of items and names them; and a main image that shows every item in the bundle and nothing that isn't included

sections.title: What we don't do
items: We can't see who physically packaged a product, or check whether a letter of authorization is valid. Where that matters, we flag it for you to confirm.
We don't log in to your account, change your listings, contact brands or file anything with Amazon.
We don't promise how Amazon will treat any listing. Only Amazon decides that.

faq.q: What is Amazon's new bundle rule?
faq.a: It's an update to Amazon's Product bundling policy that takes effect on January 11, 2027. Under it, most bundles listed as a single ASIN must be packaged by the original manufacturer or brand, with some exceptions. See [Amazon's announcement](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/seller-forums/discussions/t/da850a57-839d-4e38-a96f-298dbc450b69) for the official wording.

faq.q: What happens to bundles that don't meet it?
faq.a: Amazon says bundles that are still noncompliant after January 11 will be deactivated and become listing violations on your Account Health dashboard, and that it will notify sellers by email.

faq.q: Which Amazon store does this cover?
faq.a: Amazon posted the update on its US Seller Central forum, and we check against Amazon's US Product bundling policy. If you sell in another Amazon store, email us before you buy.

faq.q: What do I need to send you?
faq.a: The Amazon links or ASINs of your bundle listings, and which Amazon store you sell in (for example amazon.com). For the free sample, up to 5.

faq.q: Do you need my Seller Central login or password?
faq.a: No. We never ask for your password or access to your account.
The bundle listings sold under one Amazon seller account. If you're not sure, email us before you buy and we'll confirm.

faq.q: Can you guarantee Amazon will accept my listings?
faq.a: No. We review your listings carefully against the policy as Amazon has published it, but only Amazon decides how its policies apply.

faq.q: What if Amazon changes the policy?
faq.a: We check against the policy as Amazon has published it on the day we review your listings. If Amazon changes it later, your report won't reflect that change. See our [Refund Policy](/refund-policy/).

faq.q: Are you part of Amazon? Is this legal advice?
faq.a: No to both. {{name}} is an independent service, not affiliated with Amazon, and our review is not legal advice.
Click Buy and pay on Stripe's secure checkout page. If you have any trouble paying, email [{{email}}](mailto:{{email}}).

faq.q: Will I have to get on a call?
faq.a: No. There are no sales calls. Everything happens by email.

faq.q: What if something is wrong with my report?
faq.a: Email us and tell us what's wrong. We'll fix it, or refund you as our [Refund Policy](/refund-policy/) explains.
